title: Universality of e-detectors for ARL control
summary: An e-detector for a pre-change class $\mathcal P$ is a nonnegative process $M$ such that $\mathbb E_P[M_τ] \leq \mathbb E_P[τ]$ for all stopping times $τ$ and all $P \in \mathcal P$. Thresholding e-detectors controls the average run length (ARL): declaring a change at the first time $T_b$ when $M$ crosses $b$ ensures that $\inf_{P \in \mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[T] \geq b$. But e-detectors do substantially more than control the ARL; they also satisfy a \emph{optional-horizon inequality}: \[ P(T_b\leqσ)\leq \mathbb E_P[σ]/b \] for every data-dependent stopping time (monitoring horizon) \(σ\) and…
